title: Anomalous Reflection of Caustic Spin-Wave Beams in a Magnonic Waveguide
abstract: Reflection of waves at interfaces is conventionally governed by Snell's law, which follows from conservation of momentum parallel to the interface. Here we show experimentally that caustic spin-wave beams in anisotropic media obey a fundamentally different reflection mechanism. Applying time-resolved Kerr microscopy to a yttrium iron garnet waveguide, we observe that reflected beams are selected by transitions between caustic points on the anisotropic iso-frequency contour rather than by momentum conservation. As a consequence, the reflected carrier wave vector and wavefront orientation exhibit trends opposite to those predicted by Snell's law. By tuning the magnitude and orientation of an external magnetic field, we continuously control the resulting reflection process and beam routing. Our results establish caustic-point transitions as a distinct reflection law for anisotropic wave beams and provide a route towards reconfigurable magnonic beam steering.
summary: This work experimentally proves that spin-wave beams reflecting off a waveguide edge do not obey Snell's law. Instead, the reflection mechanism is dictated by transitions between caustic points on the material's anisotropic dispersion relation. This finding establishes a new physical law for magnonic beam steering and wave control.
main_problem: To demonstrate that caustic spin-wave beams reflect at an interface via a mechanism fundamentally different from conventional momentum conservation (Snell's law).
main_result: Reflection is governed by transitions between distinct caustic points on the anisotropic iso-frequency contour, leading to beam characteristics incompatible with Snell's law.
method: Time-resolved Kerr microscopy (TR-MOKE) was used experimentally to image and measure reflected spin-wave beams while systematically varying an external magnetic field.
model_or_system: The study uses a Yttrium Iron Garnet (YIG) film waveguide patterned on a GGG substrate, where spin waves propagate in an anisotropic medium.
key_observables: Reflected beam wave vector ($k_e$), wavefront orientation ($\phi_e$), and the comparison of these parameters against Snell's law predictions.
important_parameters: External magnetic field magnitude ($\mu_0H$) and angle ($\alpha_H$); the anisotropy of the material dispersion relation.
main_assumptions: The reflection process is assumed to be dictated by the geometry of caustics rather than simple momentum conservation across the boundary.
figures_summary: Figures show TR-MOKE images of reflections at waveguide edges as a function of magnetic field strength and angle, comparing observed beam parameters against theoretical predictions based on both Snell's law and caustic transitions.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the problem by contrasting conventional wave reflection with spin waves. It then presents experimental measurements using TR-MOKE to observe reflections at waveguide edges under varying external magnetic fields, systematically demonstrating deviations from Snell's law in favor of a caustic transition mechanism.
why_interesting: While focused on magnonics, the concept of anomalous wave reflection governed by geometric features (caustics) rather than simple conservation laws has parallels in advanced optics and wave physics relevant to open quantum systems modeling.
